We meet to read one paper properly rather than five badly. Each meeting is written
up here — what the paper claimed, what the room made of it, and what stayed
unresolved. New members and visitors are welcome.

::: {.next-meeting}
### Next meeting

**Tuesday 1 September 2026, 3:30 pm** · *venue to be confirmed*

**Jiadong** will discuss several papers that shaped how he thinks about the way
causal questions are posed in causal inference.

- Swales J. *The troublesome search for evidence: three cultures in need of
  integration.* J R Soc Med 93(8):402–407 (2000).
  [doi:10.1177/014107680009300804](https://doi.org/10.1177/014107680009300804) —
  a high-level, somewhat philosophical discussion of what counts as scientific
  evidence.
- Lu H, Li F, Lesko CR, *et al.* *Four targets: an enhanced framework for guiding
  causal inference from observational data.* Int J Epidemiol 54(1) (2025).
  [doi:10.1093/ije/dyaf003](https://doi.org/10.1093/ije/dyaf003) — a review
  defining the key concepts in formulating a causal question from observational
  data.
- Dickerman BA, García-Albéniz X, Logan RW, Denaxas S, Hernán MA. *Avoidable
  flaws in observational analyses: an application to statins and cancer.* Nat Med
  25(10):1601–1606 (2019).
  [doi:10.1038/s41591-019-0597-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-019-0597-x) — a
  classic paper resolving an apparent conflict between observational studies and
  meta-analyses of trials by designing the causal task properly.

Reading all three is not expected. Come anyway.
:::
